summary.headline: The Trails Committee decided to seek Community Preservation Act funds for a footbridge only, dropping a boardwalk from its fall request.
summary.summary: The Southborough Trails Committee met to finalize plans for a Community Preservation Act application ahead of the June 30 deadline for Fall Town Meeting. Members agreed to scale back the project to fund only a trail bridge, estimated at roughly $410,000 with contingencies, rather than pursuing a combined bridge and boardwalk package that would cost an estimated $630,000. The committee also planned end-of-fiscal-year budget expenditures for event equipment and maintenance supplies, reviewed boardwalk wood specifications with the Conservation Commission, and confirmed upcoming trail work parties and events.

topics.title: CPA application strategy for trail bridge and boardwalk
topics.summary: The committee discussed its Community Preservation Act (CPA) funding request due June 30 for Fall Town Meeting. Bids received in December revealed that constructing both the bridge and boardwalk would cost approximately $630,000 with escalations and contingencies, exceeding available funds. The committee reached consensus to apply only for the bridge portion, which requires roughly $145,000 to $189,000 in additional funds above the town's existing commitments.
key_details: The project has $211,000 committed from Phase 2 and approximately $44,000 remaining from Phase 1.
Total bridge construction is estimated at $410,000 after factoring in a 40% buffer for cost escalation and contingency.
A full bridge and boardwalk project was estimated to cost around $630,000.
Members decided to pursue bridge funding alone and plan to seek MassTrails grant funding to offset local costs.
Letters of support will be requested from the Recreation Commission, MWRA, and the Appalachian Mountain Club/Bay Circuit Trail.
topics.outcome: Consensus reached to submit a CPA application for the bridge only by the June 30 deadline.
topics.why_it_matters: The decision determines the scope and dollar amount of the Community Preservation Act funding request presented to voters at Fall Town Meeting.

topics.title: Interpretive signage and June 13 volunteer work party
topics.summary: Members discussed content for an additional interpretive sign and coordinated details for an upcoming volunteer work day. The committee will partner with Appalachian Mountain Club and Bay Circuit Trail volunteers to clear and construct trail around the planned boardwalk section.
key_details: Draft interpretive sign content will be circulated to committee members ahead of the next meeting.
A volunteer trail-building work party is scheduled for Saturday, June 13, starting around 9:00 AM.
Work will focus on the trail section adjacent to where the boardwalk was originally planned.
topics.outcome: Work party scheduled for June 13 at 9:00 AM.

topics.title: End-of-fiscal-year operating budget spending
topics.summary: The committee reviewed plans to spend remaining FY26 operating budget funds before the June 30 fiscal year deadline. Planned purchases include safety gear, shed storage equipment, and event outreach materials.
key_details: Approximately $3,000 remains in the committee's operating budget to be spent before June 30.
Planned purchases include disposable Tyvek suits for clearing poison ivy, shed organizers, and tool hangers.
The committee will purchase a 10x10 pop-up tent with sidewalls, a 6-foot table, chairs, sandbags, and a branded feather flag banner for Heritage Day and community outreach.
The Recreation Director confirmed purchases can be routed through town accounts to ensure tax exemption.
topics.outcome: The chair will assemble an itemized list and coordinates purchases with the Recreation Department.

topics.title: Wood treatment regulations for Town Forest boardwalk
topics.summary: The chair reported that the Conservation Commission indicated pressure-treated lumber cannot be used for an Eagle Scout boardwalk replacement project in the Town Forest, requesting heat-treated wood instead. The committee discussed wetland standards and agreed to gather technical specifications and consult regional conservation officials before making a final determination.
key_details: The Conservation Commission expressed concerns over chemical leaching near wetlands and a vernal pool.
Lumber currently stored meets American Wood Protection Association (AWPA) environmental standards for wetland use.
The chair will consult Marlborough's conservation agent, DCR, and MWRA regarding acceptable wood treatments for boardwalks in sensitive areas.
topics.outcome: The chair will compile technical wood treatment data and consult conservation staff.

topics.title: Trail maintenance and programs update
topics.summary: The committee received updates on community trail programs and trail condition issues. Yoga on the Trails launches Saturday morning with nine participants registered. Members also noted utility work mats being removed along the trail near Parkerville Road and agreed to remove deteriorating 4x4 wooden trail markers to repurpose them as sign posts.
key_details: Yoga on the Trails begins Saturday, June 6, off Parkerville Road.
Contractor mats near Deerfoot and Parkerville Road are being removed; the committee will contact National Grid to request leaving existing gravel in place to maintain a walkable surface.
Loose 4x4 trail markers that have become tripping hazards will be removed and stored for reuse as trail posts.
topics.outcome: Committee will coordinate trail cleanup and communicate trail surfacing preferences to National Grid.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes from April 9, 2026, as amended, scheduled its next meeting, and adjourned.
key_details: Minutes from April 9, 2026, were approved unanimously.
Next meeting was scheduled for Thursday, June 11, 2026, at 6:30 PM.
The meeting adjourned at 7:38 PM.
topics.outcome: April 9 minutes approved; next meeting set for June 11, 2026.
